slots.purpose: Sets how formal the copy is, from conversational to ceremonial.

references.guide: Pick one level and state it as a rule a reviewer can apply to a sentence; name what is allowed and what is not.

exemplars.note: Plain and conversational: contractions are fine, slang and in-jokes are not.
Measured and formal: no contractions, no exclamation marks, full sentences in every message.

slots.purpose: Sets how much personal warmth the copy carries.

references.guide: Describe warmth as behaviour in copy, such as whether it thanks, reassures or stays neutral.

exemplars.note: Warm but brief: thank people once, at the end of a task, never in every message.
Neutral: state facts and next steps; leave reassurance to support conversations.

slots.purpose: Sets the energy level of the copy, from calm to high-spirited.

references.guide: Tie energy to punctuation and verb choice so it can be checked.

exemplars.note: Calm: no exclamation marks, no all-caps, verbs in the present tense.
Lively on marketing pages only: one exclamation mark per page at most, none inside the product.

slots.purpose: Sets the grammatical person the copy speaks in.

references.guide: Say who 'we' and 'you' are, and when either may appear.

exemplars.note: Second person: address the reader as you; the company speaks as we only in legal and about pages.
First person plural for the team, second person for the reader, never third person for the reader.

slots.purpose: Sets the grammatical mood used for instructions and statements.

references.guide: State the mood for actions and the mood for explanations separately.

exemplars.note: Imperative for actions (Save draft), indicative for explanations (Drafts are kept for 30 days).
Indicative everywhere except buttons, which start with a verb in the imperative.

slots.purpose: Sets the target sentence length range in words.

references.guide: Give a range and the exception, such as legal prose.

exemplars.note: Interface sentences stay between 4 and 14 words; marketing body copy may reach 22.
Average 12 words per sentence; split anything over 25 words, except in legal documents.

slots.purpose: Sets the target reading level for the copy.

references.guide: Name a grade range and which surfaces may exceed it.

exemplars.note: Grade 6 to 8 for product and marketing copy; legal documents are exempt but get a plain summary.
Grade 8 at most everywhere; technical terms are allowed when the glossary defines them.

slots.purpose: Lists every brand and product name with its exact spelling and casing.

references.guide: One record per name; list accepted forms and the forms that are always wrong.

exemplars.note: Tidewell: one word, capital T only; never TideWell or TIDEWELL.
Tidewell Planner: the master name plus a plain noun; inside the app, just Planner.

slots.purpose: Lists the terms the copy prefers over common alternatives.

references.guide: Pair each preferred term with the term it replaces and the reason.

exemplars.note: Say workspace, not account, when you mean the shared place a team works in.
Say sign in, not log in or login, for the action and the button.

slots.purpose: Lists words the copy must not use, each with an alternative.

references.guide: Every avoided term needs a reason and a replacement, so the check can suggest a fix.

exemplars.note: Avoid simply and just in instructions; they make a hard step sound like the reader's fault.
Avoid users when talking to the reader; say you or name the role.

slots.purpose: Lists sentence patterns the copy must not use, as checkable rules.

references.guide: Write each pattern as a regular expression with a severity and a better alternative.

exemplars.note: No sentences that start with Please note; state the fact directly.
No click here link text; the link label names where it goes.

slots.purpose: Sets the spelling variant per locale.

references.guide: Name the locale tag and two or three words that show the variant.

exemplars.note: en-GB spelling: colour, organise, centre.
en-US spelling: color, organize, center; dates still follow the date-format rule.

slots.purpose: Records how brand and product names are pronounced, for audio and video.

references.guide: Give a simple respelling and stress, not a phonetic alphabet, unless audio vendors need it.

exemplars.note: Tidewell is said TIDE-well, two syllables, stress on the first.
Planner is said as the common word; never spell it out letter by letter.

slots.purpose: Lists the approved product claims and the Director proof each one cites.

references.guide: Each claim cites the proof cell; write two or three approved phrasings and nothing stronger.

exemplars.note: Approved: Plans sync to every device within a minute (cites the proof cell).
Approved: Works offline and catches up when you reconnect.

slots.purpose: Lists the approved numeric claims with their evidence and date.

references.guide: Every number names its source, unit and the date it was measured.

exemplars.note: Approved: Teams save about 3 hours a week, from a 2026 survey of 40 customers.
Approved: Median setup takes 12 minutes, measured across trials in the last quarter.

slots.purpose: Lists the approved compliance and regulatory statements, word for word.

references.guide: Copy compliance wording exactly as approved; record who approved it and where it may appear.

exemplars.note: Approved for footers: Payments are processed by a licensed payment provider.
Approved for sign-up: We store your data in the region you choose at sign-up.

slots.purpose: Lists the approved comparisons with alternatives, and their evidence.

references.guide: Compare with a named category, not a named competitor, unless legal has approved it.

exemplars.note: Approved: Unlike shared spreadsheets, every change keeps its author and time.
Approved: Fewer steps than a paper planner for moving a shift: two taps instead of a rewrite.

slots.purpose: Sets how numbers are written per locale.

references.guide: Cover grouping, decimals and when to spell numbers out.

exemplars.note: en: 1,250 and 3.5; spell out one to nine in prose, digits in the interface.
de: 1.250 und 3,5; always digits in the interface.

slots.purpose: Sets the plural categories each locale's messages must cover.

references.guide: List the ICU plural categories per locale and a sample message.

exemplars.note: en needs one and other: {count, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}}.
pl needs one, few, many and other; never reuse the English pair.

slots.purpose: Sets how dates are written per locale and surface.

references.guide: Give the short and long form and the rule for relative dates.

exemplars.note: Short form 30 Oct 2026, long form Friday 30 October 2026; relative dates only within 7 days.
Tables use ISO dates (2026-10-30); prose uses the long form.

slots.purpose: Sets how times and time zones are written.

references.guide: Say 12- or 24-hour, and when the zone is shown.

exemplars.note: 24-hour clock (14:30); show the time zone only when it differs from the reader's.
12-hour clock with lowercase am and pm (2:30 pm); never 2:30PM.

slots.purpose: Sets how prices and amounts are written.

references.guide: Cover symbol position, decimals and when to show the currency code.

exemplars.note: Symbol before the amount, no decimals for whole amounts: 39 a month, 39.50 when needed.
Show the ISO code after the amount on invoices: 39.00 EUR.

slots.purpose: Sets how units of measure are written.

references.guide: Name the unit system per locale and the spacing rule.

exemplars.note: Metric, with a space before the unit: 5 km, 20 kg.
Storage in GB with no space in the interface (10GB), with a space in prose (10 GB).

slots.purpose: Sets the capitalization style for headings, buttons and labels.

references.guide: Pick sentence case or title case per element and list exceptions such as brand names.

exemplars.note: Sentence case for headings, buttons and labels; brand names keep their own casing.
Title case for navigation only; everything else in sentence case.

slots.purpose: Sets punctuation rules: end marks, lists, quotes and dashes.

references.guide: Cover full stops in buttons and labels, the serial comma and dash style.

exemplars.note: No full stop on buttons, labels or headings; use the serial comma; en dash for ranges.
Curly quotes in prose, straight quotes in code; no exclamation marks in error messages.

slots.purpose: Sets text direction per locale and how mixed-direction text is handled.

references.guide: Name the right-to-left locales and the isolation rule for names and numbers.

exemplars.note: ar and he are right to left; wrap names and numbers in direction isolates.
Every locale is left to right today; new locales must declare their direction first.

slots.purpose: Sets how much room translations may need beyond the source copy.

references.guide: State the expansion ratio the source copy must leave free and where it is measured.

exemplars.note: Source copy must leave 30% room: a 40-character button holds at most 30 English characters.
German and French get 35% room on navigation labels; other surfaces keep the default 30%.
